live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a Rust-based ransomware-as-a-service gang with a short, loud history
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, sold ransomware to affiliates from late 2021. It hit hospitals, councils and big firms, and was disrupted by law enforcement before reports of an apparent exit scam in 2024.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
Malpedia describes it as a ransomware-as-a-service family written in Rust. It runs on Windows, Linux and VMware ESXi.
Malpedia says it has been seen in attacks since November 18, 2021.
Cisco Talos describes the links between the BlackMatter/DarkSide ring and BlackCat as probable. It has moderate confidence that BlackMatter affiliates were among BlackCat's early adopters.
A BlackCat representative told Recorded Future the two groups were connected but that BlackCat was not a rebrand of BlackMatter.
S2W found BlackCat's configuration fields matched BlackMatter's. It still found it difficult to conclude they were the same group.
BleepingComputer reports that the FBI estimates the group took at least $300 million in ransom payments from more than 1,000 victims up to September 2023.
Reported victims include a local government. DataBreaches reports BlackCat claimed Suffolk County's 2022 attack, which disabled the county's 911 system.
The gang listed the city of Alexandria, Louisiana as a victim. The report treats its claim of more than 80 GB of stolen data as the gang's own.

The gang also claimed attacks on firms. loanDepot confirmed a ransomware attack that exposed the data of at least 16.6 million people. BleepingComputer says ALPHV claimed it, though the gang had not yet published proof.

Recorded Future News says the gang listed India's largest drug maker, Sun Pharmaceuticals, on its leak site. It adds that the group has made a point of going after healthcare and pharmaceutical firms.
A report says AlphV claimed responsibility for the October 2023 incident at Henry Schein, a dental and medical distributor.
Sygnia attributed one 2023 case to BlackCat or one of its affiliates. Access came through a compromised third-party vendor.

In that case the attacker spent weeks moving through the network with Cobalt Strike and tunnelling tools. It copied data to cloud storage with Rclone and sent extortion emails. The client cut internet access, which stopped encryption.
eSentire reports Russian-speaking affiliates using Google ads to lure users to sites that delivered the Nitrogen malware, which led to ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware.
Malpedia says the ransomware can delete volume shadow copies, stop services and ESXi virtual machines, and spread across a network with PsExec.
Symantec reports updates in mid-2022 that added an ARM build and safe-mode encryption. Another update added searchable indexing of stolen data on the leak sites.
DataBreaches reported that the gang gave one victim, Hampton-Newport News CSB, a 48-hour deadline. The gang claimed it had stolen over 800 GB.

After the September 2023 attack on MGM Resorts, AlphV said in its own statement that it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors on September 11. The article did not verify the claim.
BleepingComputer reports that an international law enforcement operation seized the gang's Tor negotiation and leak sites in December 2023. It describes the takedown as temporary.
In February 2024, unnamed sources told BleepingComputer the Change Healthcare attack was linked to BlackCat. The site could not confirm this, and BlackCat had not claimed the attack.
UnitedHealth's SEC filing said a nation-state threat actor was behind the Change Healthcare attack. BleepingComputer notes BlackCat has not been publicly linked to any foreign government agency.

In March 2024 BleepingComputer reported that the gang appeared to be running an exit scam. Its sites were offline, affiliates said they were unpaid, and a fake FBI seizure banner appeared. Europol and the NCA said they were not involved.
A Malpedia reference list includes a December 2025 US Justice Department release. It says two Americans pleaded guilty to targeting US victims with ALPHV BlackCat ransomware.
Treat a leak-site listing as a claim until the victim or investigators confirm it.
Check what access third-party vendors have to your network, and keep backups that an intruder inside your network cannot reach.
